name: Zack Polanski
role: Leader of the Green Party of England and Wales (2025–); London Assembly member
summary: Polanski leads the Greens on an 'eco-populist' platform combining wealth taxes, rent controls, public ownership of water, and climate action. He supports drug legalisation, trans-inclusive policy, abolition of the monarchy and Lords, proportional representation, and UK withdrawal from NATO and rejoining the EU. He is a prominent critic of Israel's conduct in Gaza and describes himself as a non-Zionist Jew.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Supports abolishing the monarchy and the House of Lords.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Rejects treating government finances like a household budget and wants fiscal referees to judge whether government spends too little; this is a critique of deficit-avoidance rules, not an explicit endorsement of large deficits.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Open to citizens' assemblies, including on the House of Lords.

decide-locally.rationale: Backs subsidiarity: 'power should be at the most local possible level'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: On 2 December 2021 he proposed the London Assembly motion backing the Climate and Ecology Bill, which would require the UK Government to develop a legally binding strategy on the climate and nature emergencies, and on 1 December 2022 moved a motion for Ella's Law, a legal right to clean air; his March 2026 speech also calls for scaling up clean energy, insulation and decarbonisation by 2050.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wants the UK to begin withdrawing from NATO; also seeks new alliances 'based on peace', so this is not a rejection of all alliances.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Called the government's fiscal rules 'failing' and wants them scrapped and replaced by an expert panel of 'fiscal referees'; said the OBR 'has clearly failed'.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: States that trans women are women and trans men are men, backs gender self-ID ('Absolutely') and says Greens should seek to change the law after the Supreme Court ruling.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Reported to have called for Netanyahu to be arrested and for a full international investigation into war crimes in Gaza.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Restated support for legalising all drugs as leader, arguing the war on drugs has failed and a public health approach is needed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Calls for ending private ownership of water companies and bringing water back into public hands; defends the NHS.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Asked directly whether he would abolish the monarchy, said 'absolutely', calling it a symbol of inequality, though not his top priority.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said 'Yes, I do want to see us rejoin the European Union' and supports rejoining the customs union.

proportional-representation.rationale: At the Greens' autumn conference in 2022, as deputy leader, he said 'we need proportional representation. It's no longer a question of if – it is when', and told Keir Starmer to 'listen to your members' who had backed proportional representation.

public-ownership.rationale: Wants water returned to public hands and argues for public benefit over shareholder profit in energy, without naming energy nationalisation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: At the Greens' 2025 conference he declared that migrants and refugees are 'welcome here' and that the Greens would stop small boats through 'safe and legal routes'; in December 2025 he told The Times that people arriving in the UK 'should be able to work', calling hotels with no means of earning 'cruel'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Campaigns to 'end rip off Britain' and has called for more regulation of private corporations, a loophole-free windfall tax and an end to private profit in children's homes.

rent-control.rationale: Said 'A Green government would bring in rent controls' and backed adding them to the Renters' Rights Bill.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Called to 'end right to buy completely' and let councils buy back lost homes.

right-to-secede.rationale: Personally supports Welsh independence (leaving the decision to Wales Greens) and reportedly Scottish independence.

second-chamber.rationale: Reported to support abolishing the House of Lords; has said citizens' assemblies could decide what to do with it.

state-directs-investment.rationale: In January 2024 his London Assembly motion called on the Mayor to prioritise training workers to upgrade homes across London and to seek ongoing government funding for retrofits; he called retrofitting 'a triple win: it creates good green jobs, lowers emissions, and reduces bills'.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Proposed a 1% tax on wealth over £10m and 2% over £1bn and called it a 'day one priority'; also equalising capital gains with income tax.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pledged to 'protect our NHS' and campaigned against private-sector data involvement in it; defends a publicly funded health service.

notes:
Several sources (BBC, Guardian, The National) could not be fetched. Green Party policy was counted only where he stated it himself. Several party-wide positions (nuclear power, Trident, migration policy details, Palestine Action) were seen only in search snippets and are left null. Did not record the NATO, Israel arms embargo or Palestine Action positions as answers because no statement matches directly.

Later pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-11-14): brought to rules 7. The Wikipedia-only proportional-representation answer is re-sourced to his 2022 conference speech. Added: reduce-immigration (his Times interview and 2025 conference speech) and state-directs-investment (a London Assembly motion he moved); drastic-climate-action is re-based on the two London Assembly motions he moved. The London Assembly record was searched for motions he moved (climate and ecology bill, Zane's Law, cold homes, theatre funding, Great Smog); Zane's Law and the theatre-funding motion bear on no statement. His votes on others' motions (Churchill statue, police commendation) are press-reported only and not cited. The Sky News interview in which he calls open borders 'not pragmatic right now' could not be opened (only reports of it), so open-borders stays null.
